evidence.claim: I live at the seam between research and reality.

The throughline never changes. The hardest part of frontier technology is rarely the technology; it is the translation: scoping what is buildable now, shipping it reliably, and telling the story that makes engineers, executives and markets move together.
I take research-grade AI and turn it into things people can use, buy, and believe in.
I work the whole stack, from the protocol layer to the story.
When I am not shipping, I am reading sci-fi, thinking about robotics and the philosophy of AI, writing, and chasing a properly good cup of coffee.
I turn frontier AI research into product that ships, sells & gets used.
I think out loud on X and post the longer-form on LinkedIn.
Founder & CEO of Lilypad, a decentralised GPU network for verifiable AI inference across thousands of nodes, open-sourced when I led its wind-down in 2025, and arXiv-published.
I am endlessly curious about how minds, biological and artificial, actually work.
Previously developer relations and go-to-market at IBM and the Filecoin Foundation, and technical architecture at Accenture.

For eight-plus years I have taken the bleeding edge of AI and infrastructure and shipped it, most recently as founder and CEO of Lilypad, a decentralised GPU compute network for verifiable, trustless AI inference at scale.
I translate frontier technology into buildable scope, reliable delivery and stories that align engineers, executives and markets.
